paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. When the LORD, the God of Israel, speaks, it happens. Isaiah gives a word about Kedar with a clock on it: "Within one year, as a hired worker would count it, all the glory of Kedar will be gone." (Isaiah 21:16) And the passage ends by saying the One who spoke it is the LORD, the God of Israel. (Isaiah 21:17)

Now look at who this word touches. Dedanites out on the road, people of Tema, refugees running from war, and Kedar, a desert tribe proud of its archers. (Isaiah 21:13-17) The glory of Kedar was real, and it still had a date on it. I think that's a quiet warning, baker: what looks big and strong today is not what lasts.

But the passage isn't only about what falls. Right in the middle, people are told to act: "Bring water for the thirsty, O dwellers of Tema; meet the refugees with food." (Isaiah 21:14) Hard days were coming, and God's word still pointed people toward the thirsty and the hungry. So here's the question for you, baker: whose glory are you leaning on, and who is standing in front of you right now who needs a cup of water?
